caseno:
Civil Revision No. 2674 of 2003
with
Civil Rule No. 43(R) of 2004
lawyer:
Mr. Sheikh Zulfiquar Bulbul Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Mr. Sheikh Muhammed Serajul Islam with Mr. Md. KalimuIlah Mazumder, Advocate ----- For the opposite parties.
parties:
Md. Siddiqur rahman and others
Vs.
Sheikh alauddin and others
full_judgment:
Borhaauddin, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17.09.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. Manshigonj, in Title Appeal no.41 of 2000 affirming those of dated 31.01.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj, in Title Suit no.61 of 1996 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party no.1 herein as plaintiff instituted Civil Suit no.61 of 1996 impleading the opposite party nos.2-6 as defendants for declaration of title. Plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land originally belonged to C.S. recordee Bhagirathi Das who sold the suit land including other lands to Sree Kamini Kumar Chakraborty. Sree Subodh Debnath, Sreemoti Sailabala Debi by three separate deeds all dated 15.03.1954. Accordingly S.A. Khatian recorded in their names. Said Subodh Debnath and others sold out the same to Abdul Rahman Bepari by deed dated 21.07.1970. Abdul Rahman Bepari sold the suit land measuring .07½ sataks including other lands to Md. Habibullah and Most. Jahanara vide two registered deed dated 11.08.1975. Abdul Rahman sold and handed over exclusive possession of the land of suit S.A. Plot no.476 corresponding to latest Settlement Plot no.410 to the purchasers by the aforesaid deed. Abdul Rahman sold out other lands apart from suit land by sale deed no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 to other persons and in the said deeds though S.A. Plot no.476 corresponding to latest Settlement plot no.410 written but actually they have been in possession of .38 sataks land which are not suit land. Abdul Rahman Bepari, Md. Habibullah and Jahanara Begun sold out their purchased land to Most. Amena Khatun by registered deed dated 20.11.1976 who transferred the land in favour of the plaintiff by Heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 16.08.1990. Thus the plaintiff acquired absolute right, title and interest in the suit land by deed of Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16„08.1990. Plaintiff came to know from the office of the Assistant Commissioner (land) on 10.11.1995 that .51 Sataks of land of R.S. Plot no.410 under R.S. Khatian no.49 has been recorded in the name of Sreenagar Thana Parishad. Said wrong and illegal entry of record creates cloud upon the title of the plaintiff. Hence, the present suit.

3. The defendant nos.6-7 added themselves in the suit by order no.29 dated 02.6.1978. Defendant nos.1-5 and defendant nos.6-7 contested the suit by filing separate written statement.

4. The case of the defendant nos.1-5 is that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and the suit is liable to be dismissed for want of cause auction. Further contending that the suit land is the Government khas land and the S.A. recorded owner did not transfer the same to any person. Abdul Rahman Bepari created a false deed dated 21.07.1970 and R.S. Khatian for .15 Sataks of land wrongly recorded in the name of Abdul Rahman Bepari who had no legal right to transfer the suit land. They prayed for dismissal of the suit.

5. The Case of the defendant nos.6 and 7 is that the land in C.S. Plot no.476 under C.S. khatian no.242 including other lands belonged to Bhagirathi Das who sold out the same to Kamini Kumar Chakraborty, Sree Subodh Kumar Chakraborty and Sreemoti Amia Bala Debi vide sale deed dated 20.11.1945 and delivered possession thereof. S.A. Khatian finally recorded in the name of Sudhir Kumer Chakraborty for 6(six) annas, Subodh Chandra Debnath for 4(four) annas and Sremoti Sailabala Debi for 6(six) annas and they in their turn sold out the suit land including other lands to Abdul Rahman by registered deed dated 21.07.1970 and delivered possession thereof. R.S. Khatian has been finally published in the name of Abdul Rahman and he in his turn sold out .38 sataks of suit land vide deed no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 to Abdul Latif Laskar who died leaving one son Abdul Majid Laskar, two minor daughters namely Salma Khatun and Shahnaj Begum and wife Most. Masuda Khatun as heirs. The heirs of said Abdul Latif Laskar sold out their inherited property to Narayan Chandra Saha and Madhab Chandra Saha vide registered deed dated 30.05.1985. Said Narayan Chandra Saha and Madhab Chandra Saha jointly sold out .38 Sakats suit land to A. Majid and A. Sattar vide registered deed dated 01.07.1985. A. Majid died leaving 2(two) sons namely Md. Monir Hossain and Md. Panir Hossain and wife Ripana Akter who in their turn sold out the land to Sheikh Dalil, Most. Angura Begum, Sheikh Khalil and Most. Bedana Begum vide deed dated 17.04.1995 who also in their turn sold out .38 sataks of land to the added defendant nos.6 and 7 vide deed dated 17.05.1998 and delivered possession thereof. 'Thus the defendant nos.6-7 acquired absolute right, title and interest in the suit land of .38 Sataks and are in peaceful possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. Record in the name of Thana Parishad in wrong, in-operative and ineffective. Plaintiff's case is false, concocted and fabricated and the plaintiff was never in possession of the suit land. With such averments they prayed for dismissal of the suit.

6. During trial the plaintiff examined 7 witnesses and the defendant nos.6-7 examined 6 witnesses to prove their respective cases but the defendant nos.1-5 did not produce or examine any witness.

7. Upon hearing the parties, the learned Sub-judge, 2nd court, Munshigonj, decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 31.01.2000.

8. Being aggrieved the added defendant nos.6-7 preferred Title Appeal no.31 of 2000 in the court of learned District Judge, Munshigonj. On transfer the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Munshigonj, who after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 17.09.2000 and thus affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj.

9. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, the added defendant nos.6 and 7 as petitioners preferred the instant revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present rule and order of stay.

10. Mr. Sheikh Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the courts below failed to appreciate that Abdul Rahman bepari sold out .07½ Sataks suit land to Md. Habibullah and Most Jahanra vide deed dated 11.08.1975 and Md. Habibullah and Most. Jahanara in their turn sold the same to Amena Khatun by whom the plaintiff acquired right, title and interest of the suit land and as such the plaintiff cannot claim more than .07½ Sataks land, without considering this factual aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law which occasioned failure of justice. He also submits though in the sale deed nos.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 it is written that .38 sataks of land from the suit plot was sold to the added defendants no.6 and 7 but in the oral evidence the P.Ws. deposed that they are in possession of the suit land. In this regard by referring section 92 of the Evidence Act. Mr. Chowdhury submits that written contents of the documents will prevail upon oral evidence. He also submits that for rectification of a deed under section 31 of the Specific Relief Act. four conditions needs to be fulfilled which are absent in the pleading of the plaintiff. lie further submits that in view of section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act. and section 47 of the Registration Act. earlier registered deed will prevail upon the subsequent deed for the selfsame property. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Firoza Mozid and another vs-Jiban Bima Corporation, reported in 39 DLR (AD) 78; the case of Joynal Abedin Molla vs- Aliar Rahman and others, reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 105; the case of Habibullah and others —vs- Md. Solaiman and others, reported in 6 Bangladesh Supreme Court Digest 187 and the case of Begum Jan and others vs-Moklesur Rahman, reported in 6 BLC 580.

11. On the other hand Mr. Sheikh Muhammed Serajul Islam with Mr. Md. Kalmullah Mazumder, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party no.1 by filing counter affidavit submits that the courts below arrived at a concurrent findings of fact that the added defendant nos.6-7 are not in possession of .38 Sataks of land in S.A. Plot no.476 corresponding to latest Settlement Plot no.410. He also submits that both the courts below arrived at a concurrent findings of fact that the vendor of the plaintiff purchased the suit schedule land from Jahanara, Habibullah and Abdul Rahman vide registered deed dated 20.11.1976. He further submits that decisions of the court of appeal being last and final court of fact are not open to interference in revisional jurisdiction unless it is shown that the same have been based upon gross misreading of evidence or founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or of any mis-interpretation of any material document or otherwise perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials on record. He submits that the concurrent findings of fact based on evidence cannot be disturbed in revisional jurisdiction. He also submits that there is no ambiguity or infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Mazharul Borhan —vs- A. H. Bhuiyan, reported in 15 BLD(AD) 237 and the case of Shambhu Nath Poddar —vs-Bangladesh Railway and others, reported in 43 DLR(AD)82.

12. Heard the learned Advocates. Perused the revisional application, judgment of the courts below and the materials available in the lower court record.

13. I have carefully gone through the judgment passed by the courts below. The learned Subordinate Judge framed the following issues to dispose of the suit:

"(1)Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form?

(2) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?

(3) Is the suit bad for defect of parties?

(4) Has the plaintiff right, title and interest in the suit?

5) What other reliefs the plaintiffs are entitled to get?"

<u>14. Upon threadbare discussions on the issues the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit holding that the vendor of the plaintiff Amena Khatun purchased the suit land from Jahanara Begum, Habibullah and Abdul Rahman by registered deed dated 20.11.1976 and said Amena Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff vide Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16.08.1990 which are proved by Exhibit-7, 8, 10 and 11. From Exhibit-"Kha-and "Kha(1)" produced by the added defendant nos.6-7 it is apparent that in the deed nos.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 the quantum of land is .38 sataks in S.A. Plot no.476 and on the north of the suit land the possessor is Gunjar Ali. But on perusal of S.A. Khatian no.242 it appears that the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is 66 sataks and on the north of the land the possessor is Razzab Ali and as such by the said deeds the suit land was not transferred in favour of the added defendants because the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is not 38 sataks. But total land sold by the deed nos.629 and 630 is .38 sataks and on the north the possessor is Gunjar Ali. The added defendants also produced DCR and one rent receipt marked as Exhibit 'ka' and 'ka-1' which also shows that the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is .38 sataks. It is not mentioned in the Exhibits .38 sataks out of 66 sataks. Thus the Trial Court held that the suit land was not transferred by the deeds no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.105. The Trial Court also discussed the evidence of the P.Ws. and D.Ws. P.W. I stated in his deposition that Amena Khatun purchased the suit land from Jahanara, Habibullah and Abdul Rahman vide deed dated 20.11.1976 and since then the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land on behalf of her daughter Amena Khatun. After purchase of the suit land Amena Khatun paid rents to the Government exchequer in the name of Sudhir Chandra Deb Nath and thereafter Amena Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of her father i.e. the present plaintiff by Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16.08.1990. This P.W. also stated that .51 Sataks of their land recorded as .53 Sataks in the name of Thana Parishad which is wrong and illegal. P.W.1 was cross-examined by added defendant nos.6-7 but failed to shaken her. The trial court also examined the defendants' witnesses. D.W.1 stated in his cross-examination that " আমি উত্তর পাশ দিয়া নালিশী জমি দাবী করিয়াছি।" He stated that in the south of his land the plaintiff is cultivating his land. He also stated that he does not aware whether the plaintiff is a land owner or borgadar. D. Ws. 2, 3 and 4 stated in their deposition that on a tree besides the suit land a signboard is hanging in the name of Siddiqur Rahman. D.W.5 stated in his deposition that in a tree besides the suit land a signboard carrying the names of Siddiqur and Siraj is hanging. By discussing the oral and documentary evidence the trial court arrived at a finding that the plaintiff has been able' to prove his case and thus decreed the suit. On perusal of the judgment passed by the appellate court below, it appears that the learned Additional District Judge after re-assessing the evidence on record independently dis-allowed the appeal and thus affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. It also appears that the Additional District Judge on perusal of the Exhibits-7, 8, 10 and 11 arrived at a finding that the plaintiff-respondent is in possession of the suit land. He also assessed the exhibit- "Kha" and "Kha(1)" produced by the added defendant appellants along with S.A. Khatian no.242 wherein the quantum of land mentioned against S.A. Plot no.476 is 66 sataks and on the north the possessor is Razzab Ali. But in the deeds i.e. Exhibit `kha' and `kha-1' the quantum of land is .38 sataks and on the north the possessor is Gunjar AIi Thus the appellate court below also arrived at a finding that by Exhibit `kha' and 'kha-1', the suit land was not transferred in favour of defendants no.6 and 7.</u>

<u>15. On perusal of the evidence on record both the courts below arrived at a finding that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land.</u>

<u>16. Now it is settled position of law that when the court below gives a decision on the basis of documentary evidence that is a question of fact and this court ordinarily should not be interfered with the question of fact arrived by a court below unless it appears that the court below patently committed illegality and took wrong view of law.</u>

17. It is well settled principle of law that under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure the High Court cannot re-appreciate the evidence and cannot set aside the concurrent findings of the courts below by taking a different view of the evidence. The High Court is empowered only to interfere with the findings of fact, if the findings are perverse or there has been a non appreciation or non-consideration of the material evidence on record by the courts below. Simply because another view of the evidence may be taken is no ground by the High Court to interfere in its revisional jurisdiction.

18. Going through the impugned judgment and decree, I do not find any findings of fact recorded by the court below are perverse and there has been non-application of mind.

19. Under the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the learned Additional District Judge, Munshigonj, has not committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of the justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 17.09.2000 passed in Title Appeal no. 41 of 2000 and as such there is nothing to interfere with the same.

20. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

21. The connected Civil Rule no. 43(R) / 04 is disposed of accordingly.

22. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is vacated and accordingly the ad-interim order passed in Civil Rule ho.43(R)/04 is also hereby vacated.

23. The facts and circumstances of the cases referred by the learned Advocate for the. petitioners are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.

24. Send down the lower court record.

End.
